title: Instance documents may deviate from general processes even though Agent customizations may only extend Core logic
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.3 describes the Instance-specific Operational Processes slot as containing "operational procedures or monitoring requirements unique to this Instance that **deviate from or otherwise supplement** the general Spark Liquidity Layer processes."

Compare the equivalent slot one level up. Agent Customizations documents (A.6.1.1.1.2.5.1.2.1.2.1.1 and A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.2.1.1) permit an Agent only to "**extend** the baseline functionality defined in the Sky Core Atlas ... layered on top of the inherited Sky Core logic," and require that "any extensions must remain fully aligned with the requirements specified in the Sky Core Atlas."

The two verbs differ in kind. Extension preserves the guarantees of the base: whatever the Core logic promised still holds, plus more. Deviation does not — a deviating Instance may do something the general process forbids or omit something it requires, and nothing in this provision names an approval step, an alignment test, or a party who checks.

The practical consequence is that a reader cannot rely on the general Spark Liquidity Layer procedures being true of any particular Instance. Every ICD must be read for local overrides, which weakens the main benefit of writing procedures once per interface standard.

Whether this is an inconsistency or a considered choice is not resolvable from the text. Venue-specific realities plainly do sometimes require departure from a generic procedure. But the asymmetry — extend-only against the parent framework, deviate-freely against the Agent's own — puts the looser rule exactly where the concrete money movements happen.
description: Each ICD's Instance-specific Operational Processes slot admits procedures that 'deviate from or otherwise supplement' Spark's general processes
